title: Closed-fibre specialization and local algebra preparation for a smooth pair
statement: Let $A_0$ be a Noetherian integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], $T=\operatorname{Spec}A_0$, and $g:V=\operatorname{Spec}B_0\to T$ smooth of finite presentation [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Let $Z\subseteq V$ be closed. Its inverse image in each fibre contains no irreducible component [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-residue-field, def-weil-irreducible-components], and every point of $Z_\eta$ has local ring of dimension at least two in $V_\eta$, where $\eta$ is the generic point of $T$ [def-sc-generic-point, def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. For every $z\in Z$ there is a point $y\in Z_{g(z)}$ closed in the fibre $V_{g(z)}$ [def-weil-closed-points] to which the fibre point $z$ specializes (meaning $y$ lies in its closure). Write $s=g(z)=g(y)$, $A=\mathcal O_{T,s}$, $B=\mathcal O_{V,y}$ and $\mathfrak m_A$ for the maximal ideal of $A$. Then $A$ and $B$ are Noetherian local rings, the actual stalk map $A\to B$ is local and formally smooth for the maximal-ideal adic topology on $B$ [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic], $\kappa(y)/\kappa(s)$ is finite, and $\dim B>\dim A$. The ideal $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak m_AB$ is prime. The point $z$ defines a prime $\mathfrak q_z\subset B$ with $\mathfrak p\subsetneq\mathfrak q_z$, and there is a canonical isomorphism $B_{\mathfrak q_z}\cong\mathcal O_{V,z}$ of local rings [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Moreover $\dim B_{\mathfrak q_z}\ge2$.

source.place: EGA IV4 Proposition 21.14.3(ii), final proof paragraph: closed specialization y in the fibre, formal smoothness 17.5.3, dimension 17.5.8, residue extension I 6.4.2, and the prime corresponding to z. Dimension >=2 also uses generic-fibre codimension and flat local dimension. Read in the online English EGA translation; local EGA IV4 WANTED.

proof.text: Write $\sigma\subset A_0$ for $s=g(z)$ and $Q_z\subset B_0$ for $z$. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine], $A_0\to B_0$ is a smooth ring map, hence has a finite polynomial presentation by [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]. Therefore $B_0$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], $V_s=\operatorname{Spec}C$, where $C=B_0\otimes_{A_0}\kappa(s)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-fibre-regular-local], $C$ is smooth over $\kappa(s)$ and its prime localizations are regular local rings. In particular $C$ is finite type over that field. The fibre projection identifies its underlying space with $g^{-1}(s)$ by [def-pc-scheme-fibre].

The closure $H=\overline{\{z\}}$ in $\operatorname{Spec}C$ is nonempty and lies in the closed inverse image $Z_s$. The closed points of $\operatorname{Spec}C$ lying in $H$ are dense in $H$ by [lem-sc-lft-over-field-jacobson-space], so at least one exists; choose it as $y$. Thus $y\in Z_s$ is closed in the whole fibre and is a specialization of $z$. Let $M\subset C$ be its maximal ideal. Its residue field is $C/M$, a finitely generated $\kappa(s)$-algebra because it is a quotient of $C$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-zariski-lemma] to conclude $[\kappa(y):\kappa(s)]<\infty$. Here $\kappa(y)$ as a fibre point and as a point of $V$ agree: the stalk quotient of [lem-sbc-scheme-fibre-stalk-quotient] has kernel in the maximal ideal, so taking its residue field gives the same quotient by the maximal ideal.

Let $Q_y\subset B_0$ be the prime for $y$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], $A=\mathcal O_{T,s}\cong(A_0)_\sigma$ and $B=\mathcal O_{V,y}\cong(B_0)_{Q_y}$ through their actual germ maps. These are local rings by [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] and step 1. The actual stalk map is local, as stated in [def-weil-flat-morphism]. By [lem-sfb-smooth-stalk-formally-smooth] it has the square-zero lifting property for every $A$-algebra map $B\to D/J$, without a continuity condition. Applying that property to the maps which kill a power of the maximal ideal gives exactly [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic]. Thus the stalk map is formally smooth for the required maximal-ideal adic topology.

source.place: Tag 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence); smooth-stalk lifting via Tags 04EG, 031H and more-morphisms.tex 02H6; adic definition more-algebra.tex 07NI.

proof.text: Put $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak m_AB$. By [lem-sbc-scheme-fibre-stalk-quotient], $B/\mathfrak p\cong\mathcal O_{V_s,y}$, and $\mathcal O_{V_s,y}\cong C_M$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] applied to $V_s=\operatorname{Spec}C$ (step 1); likewise $\mathcal O_{V_s,w}\cong C_{P_w}$ for every $w\in V_s$ with prime $P_w\subset C$. The ring $C_M$ is regular local by step 1 and is a nonzero integral domain by [lem-sc-regular-local-domain]. Consequently $\mathfrak p$ is prime: a product in its kernel maps to zero in a domain, and one factor maps to zero. We will use this same fibre-stalk identification at other points of $V_s$.

For each $w\in Z_s$, let $P_w\subset C$ be its prime. It is not a minimal prime of $C$: otherwise [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-components-minimal-primes] makes $V(P_w)$ a fibre component, while $Z_s$, being closed and containing $w$, contains $\overline{\{w\}}=V(P_w)$, contrary to the hypothesis. By [lem-weil-pbc-prime-contains-minimal-prime], there is a minimal prime $N_w\subsetneq P_w$. The prime-localization correspondence in [lem-weil-pbc-localization-prime-residue-field-iso] preserves this strict inclusion in $C_{P_w}$: their contractions are the distinct original primes. Hence $\dim C_{P_w}\ge1$ directly from [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. This applies both to $w=y$ and to $w=z$.

The ring map $A_0\to B_0$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-flat]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-height-formula] at $Q_y$ and $Q_z$; both contract to $\sigma$. With the stalk identifications of steps 3 and 4 ([lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] for $\mathcal O_{V,z}\cong(B_0)_{Q_z}$ and $\mathcal O_{V_s,z}\cong C_{P_z}$), it gives
$$\dim\mathcal O_{V,w}=\dim A+\dim\mathcal O_{V_s,w}\qquad(w=y,z).$$
The base local dimension is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-finite-krull-dimension]. Step 5 now gives $\dim B\ge\dim A+1>\dim A$. This uses the dimension of the fibre local ring, not the topological local dimension of the fibre at a nonclosed point.

Since $y$ specializes from $z$ in $V_s$, it also does so in $V$, and $Q_z\subseteq Q_y$. Explicitly $\overline{\{Q_z\}}=V(Q_z)$: a closed $V(I)$ contains $Q_z$ precisely when $I\subseteq Q_z$, and their intersection is $V(Q_z)$. Define $\mathfrak q_z=Q_zB$. The localization correspondence in [lem-weil-pbc-localization-prime-residue-field-iso] shows this is prime, with contraction $Q_z$. Since $\sigma B_0\subseteq Q_z$, we have $\mathfrak p\subseteq\mathfrak q_z$. Equality is impossible: modulo $\mathfrak p$, the prime $\mathfrak q_z/\mathfrak p$ is the localization of $P_z$ in $C_M$, and the strict chain $N_z\subsetneq P_z$ from step 5 survives in $C_M$ (both primes lie under $M$). It cannot end in the zero prime, which has no strictly smaller ideal. Therefore $\mathfrak p\subsetneq\mathfrak q_z$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localize-localization-at-prime](1),
$$B_{\mathfrak q_z}\cong(B_0)_{Q_z}\cong\mathcal O_{V,z},$$
the last isomorphism being [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization]. The maps send each fraction to the same fraction, so this is the canonical local-ring isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 00E3 (lemma-spec-localization); schemes.tex Tag 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves); the comparison is the iterated localization at the prime of z.

proof.text: It remains to show $\dim\mathcal O_{V,z}\ge2$. If $s\ne\eta$, the prime $\sigma$ is nonzero since $A_0$ is a domain. The strict chain $(0)\subsetneq\sigma$ survives in $(A_0)_\sigma$ by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-prime-residue-field-iso], so $\dim A\ge1$. Combine step 6 at $z$ with step 5 to get $\dim\mathcal O_{V,z}\ge1+1=2$. If $s=\eta$, then $\sigma=(0)$ and $A=(A_0)_{(0)}=\operatorname{Frac}(A_0)=\kappa(\eta)$ is a field. The fibre stalk quotient [lem-sbc-scheme-fibre-stalk-quotient] therefore identifies $\mathcal O_{V,z}$ with $\mathcal O_{V_\eta,z}$. Its dimension is at least two by the generic-fibre hypothesis of the item. Finally use step 7 to obtain $\dim B_{\mathfrak q_z}\ge2$.

Stacks sources checked: 0HA1 at schemes.tex l.3545 and 0478(2) at varieties.tex l.2670. EGA IV4 21.14.3(ii) is not in literature/, so it is flagged WANTED and proof_origin is agent. Statement and stmt_deps are unchanged from base, there are no new nodes, and there is no re-split note. The statement is true; checked on k[t]⊂k[t,u] with Z=V(t,u), on k⊂k[u,v], and on the vacuous case k⊂k[u] with Z=V(u). The eight steps are correct. Step 2 takes a closed y in the closure of z in the fibre by Jacobson density, then gets a finite residue extension by Zariski's lemma. Step 3 restricts the lifting of lem-sfb-smooth-stalk-formally-smooth to maps killing m^k, which is the adic definition. Step 4 gets B/m_A B regular local, hence a domain, so p is prime. Step 5 uses the no-component hypothesis to show the fibre prime is not minimal, so the fibre local dimension is at least 1. Step 6 applies the flat height formula 00ON. Step 7 proves p strictly inside q_z through the surviving chain N_z⊊P_z and gets B_{q_z}≅O_{V,z} by iterated localization. Step 8 splits s≠η (dim A≥1) from s=η (the generic codimension-2 hypothesis). These conclusions match what the parent feeds into lem-sfb-formally-smooth-ramanujam-samuel-localization. No duplicate found (rg -L for 21.14.3 and for the no-component phrase). The only off-route citation is lem-sbc-scheme-fibre-stalk-quotient (sk-thm-vanishing), declared and accepted as a generic tool use; the p1, picard and reduction citations are in the unit's transitive route.
